# New year, new version: Firebird 1.6

**New features:**
* New dialog for creating Flash images, which is also available in the Mobile UI! (#262) 
* Running as 64bit application on Windows is supported now (#234)
* Polish translation is available now (#207)
* CX II (/-T/CAS) calculators can now be emulated (#165)! However, with the current dumping programs you will not get a complete bootrom and booting the OS will fail.

**Improvements:**
* Multiple files can be sent in the Mobile UI and by dropping them into the main window on desktop (#279)
 Reimplemented emulation speed control: Now it's more accurate, especially on Windows
* GitHub actions now performs automated builds for Android (armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a in one APK), macOS and Windows (32bit and 64bit) on releases and pull requests (#283, #284, #285)
* The "installer" for OS 4.5.3.14 (and later?) works now. It requires [fastboot RAM](https://hackspire.org/index.php?title=Memory-mapped_I/O_ports_on_CX#90030000_-_Fastboot_RAM) to persist state across reboots, which is now implemented.
* More accurate emulation of the On button: It's now possible to enter Press-To-Test mode (#271)
* Faster saving and loading of snapshots (#231)
* More reliable USB file transfers
* The debugger console now includes entered commands in the log
* Support for PIE (position-independent executables) on x86_64. Previously, care needed to be taken that PIE was disabled, otherwise it would crash on start. (#211)
* Building the JIT is disabled automatically if the platform does not support it (#197)
* Firebird builds on FreeBSD now (#228, #248)

**Bugfixes:**
* File access on Android got fixed (#202 and its various duplicates)
* Fix placement of keypad buttons in the touchpad area (#41)
* Various fixes for the Mobile UI layout (#201)
* The kit configuration page in the Mobile UI no longer causes the keyboard to pop up by default (#257)
* Connecting with GDB on windows works now (#259, #260)
* Some shades of grey were not displayed properly when emulating pre-CX models (#270)
* Fix crash on AArch64/arm64 when executing certain instructions
* The keypad reacts to touch events in the desktop version as well now (#292, #293)
* Some places were no longer translated correctly after the introduction of language switching in 1.5
* Keys could get stuck on focus changes. Now they're all released when the keypad loses focus (#287)
* The Ctrl key now changes color when pressed
* Emulation speed no longer remains unlimited after a failed file transfer

_Repo for Arch, Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu and openSUSE: [via OBS](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=home%3AVogtinator%3Afirebird-emu&package=firebird-emu&locale=en)._

There is work in progress to implement and improve support for running in the browser on Qt for WebAssembly (#294). A preview is available on https://nspire-emus.github.io/firebird/wasm/

NOTE: BundleIdentifier changed in this version and automatic updates have been disabled until manual install occurs.

apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 emulator for ARM64
apps.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Android: regenerate the PGO profile on the source with the GS runs build
- tests: the block hasher's unaligned update stays inside the test memory
- GS: comments that named removed gsrunner switches, and an include they needed
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine's development log goes
- GS/TC: the lean path's mode switch and check halves go
- gsrunner: the burst memo's switches and statistics line go
- gsrunner: the readback lane's statistics, trace and switches go
- gsrunner: the kick's two check modes go
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine sleeps where runs do not form
- GS: the vertex buffer grows in 64-bit sizes and fails loudly past a ceiling
- GS: a reset of the draw buffers frees the buffers it replaces
- GS/SW: a draw whose frame and Z buffers share pages is not split between workers
- GS/SW: a texture is not refilled while a queued draw still reads it
- GS/Vulkan: a run that holds a large draw keeps one state for all its draws
- GS/Vulkan: a draw that cannot open a run is primed before it is classified
- GS/Vulkan: the stencil counter resolve pipeline takes blend constants and line width dynamic

apps.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

This build brings everything since 0.1.634: external drives, Windows Vulkan for 64-bit games (experimental, per game), Ubisoft Connect with Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4, a native interface for the foldable iPhone (experimental), colour profiles, many Direct3D 9, 11 and 12 fixes, Steam (BCD Dock) fixes, recommended settings for 60 more games and over 150 new Auto-tune rules.

## New

- **New icon:** BCD has a new app icon by Mila (mudcatpot), with versions for iOS's dark and tinted home screens. Thank you, Mila!
- **External drives:** **Settings › Storage › External drives › Add a drive or folder** adds a drive (a USB-C SSD or a stick) or a folder on it; you can add several. Each drive appears in Windows as `C:\External\<name>` and as a drive letter.
  - **Find games** adds the games on a drive to your library, and the drive's Steam libraries are found by themselves: their games start through BCD Dock like any other Steam game.
  - A Steam game's page offers **External drive** for a new install (**Steam installs** in the same settings picks the default place), and Steam updates and repairs a game in the library it lives in.
  - **Location › Move to** on a game's page moves a Steam game, or a game you added from Files, between the device and a drive: it copies the game, checks the copy, then deletes the original. The game keeps its settings, Workshop items and launch options.
  - Before a download, files already on the disk are checked once, so a repaired or moved game is not downloaded again.
  - The earlier External SSD folder becomes a drive by itself, with its games and their settings. If it does not open at the first start, BCD tries again at the next start or at Play.
  - **Reconnect** opens a drive again after it was unplugged; **Remove** forgets it.
- **Windows Vulkan (experimental, 64-bit games):** a game's page has **Direct3D › Vulkan (experimental)**. With it, a 64-bit game that draws with Vulkan gets Vulkan through MoltenVK (`vulkan = moltenvk`). Off by default; turn it on per game.
- **Ubisoft Connect, Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4:**
  - Ubisoft Connect no longer stops right after its start.
  - Its built-in browser runs with fewer processes, so it fits.
  - Its installer is not run again for every Ubisoft game once the launcher is installed.
  - A game started through it gets the settings the launcher needs for that session only.
  - Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4 have recommended settings.
- **Foldable iPhone (experimental):** **Settings › Graphics › Foldable iPhone** has two switches, both off by default and both changing nothing on other iPhones and iPads.
  - **Duo enhancements** gives BCD a native interface with Liquid Glass, system tabs and a sidebar, search in the Library and controller navigation. The Windows desktop's Start, Open and Stop sit on Home, and downloads resume when the desktop runs in the background.
  - **Foldable iPhone support** starts a game you add at a resolution shaped like the inner display, and the touch controls follow the screen when you fold or unfold the phone.
  - Installed directly, iOS shows BCD in a small window on the inner display; inside LiveContainer it fills the screen. Both switches apply from the next start of BCD.
- **Colour profiles:** **Settings › Appearance** picks BCD's colours. The default look is unchanged.
- **Xbox 360 controller identity:** **Controls › Controller API › Xbox 360 controller (XInput + device)** on a game's page keeps the XInput pad and also lists it as an Xbox 360 controller, for a game that shows no controller otherwise (Far Cry 4).
- **Aim with a stick:** an aim zone can drive the right stick instead of the mouse (**Aim mode › The finger moves › The right stick** on a game's page), for a game that ignores the mouse while a controller is in use (NieR).

## Fixes and improvements

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** A game keeps the settings it had until you reset them. On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**, then check that **Options › Auto-tune › Auto-tune this game** is on, and start the game again.

Each fix targets the error a log showed; a game may now get further and still stop at a later point. If it does, please send a new log: it names the next problem.

### Games

Every game a log, a report or a test reached since 0.1.634. Where a game is not fixed, its line says which stop it passes now or which stop is named, and where it stops next when a log shows that.

#### Fixed in code

The stop the log showed cannot happen the same way any more. Almost none of these could be tried on a device yet, so a game may now get further and stop at a later point; where a log shows where that is, it is said.

- **1000xRESIST:** the Unity IL2CPP garbage collector raced with the game and ended it after 14 to 15 repairs of the same three virtual calls, about 16 seconds in at 54 FPS (the earlier frame-context experiment did not help). The repair has a fourth pass now that takes the object's class word and proves the table before it writes; and the recommended settings make the collector really suspend the game's threads (as for Megabonk, Big Walk, BALL x PIT and Lonely Mountains). Fixed for that fault; not tested on a device yet.
- **Age of Wonders 4:** the game asked Metal for a multisampled view of a single-sample texture and Metal's validation ended the game. The view now takes the texture's own type. Fixed.
- **Alan Wake:** about 67 Direct3D 9 pipelines per run were refused by the graphics driver, because a vertex shader that writes the point size was used in triangle draws; those draws were missing. The point size is now written only in point draws. Fixed. Text in a sent log's comment also no longer counts as the game's own log lines (it had produced a false "known stop"). For the crash at the end of a run, where BCD itself ended while a game thread exited, two experiments exist for the game's own settings, off by default: `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_DIAG = 1` names the object and `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP = 1` skips that clean-up.
- **Assassin's Creed (2007):** it died after Steam's helper program unloaded and cleared the game's thread-local data. A program's `TlsFree` now clears slots only in its own program's threads, as on Windows (`env.MADEIRA_TLS_CLEAR_OWN_PROCESS = 0` brings the old behaviour back). Fixed.
- **Battlefield 2 and Cold Fear:** the shader converter did not know the compressed-normal vertex formats DEC3N and UDEC3 and stopped the game, Battlefield 2 about 40 seconds in and Cold Fear at its first 3D scene. Both formats are converted now. Fixed. Battlefield 2 with a Direct3D wrapper in its folder can also stop on a stale memory alias; Auto-tune now tries the setting that releases stale memory aliases for it.
- **BioShock:** the game stopped about 110 seconds after the logos, when its renderer thread read a NULL getter right after the first run-time HLSL compiles. Wine's D3DX compile functions never wrote the result variable (`pHResult`) that the game passes; the six functions now write it as Windows documents. This is the likely cause, not proved; if it still stops, the log now holds the compiler's text for every failed compile (24 per process, with the first 160 bytes of the source). The recommended settings keep a file trace of 20,000 lines so the name of the shader-error file shows. For "no sound after the intro", `env.MADEIRA_AUDIO_CAPTURE = 1` (off by default; put it in the game's own settings) offers one silent recording device, never the microphone and never mixed.
- **Black Mesa:** its own crash handler closes the game with exit code 1 after 17 seconds, and the BCD Dock session stayed open on a dead picture. A game that closes within 30 seconds without a picture now ends its session, whatever its exit code. Fixed. The crash itself (a call from Qt's QML engine into an empty page) is not fixed; the log now says whether BCD's views of that page agree.
- **Blur:** the game's protected start-up code uses an x86 bit-scan with a redundant prefix that the emulator rejected ("Invalid instruction"). That form and a few similar ones now decode. Fixed; the stub may stop at its next instruction.
- **Bulletstorm, Hitman: Blood Money, Medal of Honor: Airborne and LEGO Marvel Super Heroes** (BCD Dock): the 32-bit game said Steam was not running (error 113, "Problem starting up Steam") because the Dock wrote Steam's entries only where 64-bit programs read them. They are now also written where a 32-bit game reads them (an entry of a client that is gone is overwritten for the session). Fixed. Bulletstorm's recommended settings also dump the registers at its start-up fault; started directly, Hitman: Blood Money shows "Failed to find Steam", which Auto-tune now answers with "start it with BCD Dock".
- **Capcom games** (Resident Evil 3, Resident Evil 4, Resident Evil Requiem, Monster Hunter Rise, Monster Hunter Stories 3 trial, Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection, Onimusha): their first start ran only Capcom's codec notice, a .NET program that cannot run under Wine Mono and installs nothing, then asked you to restart BCD. BCD now treats that notice as provided, so the first Play starts the game. Fixed. For Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection and Monster Hunter Rise, whose packed program then stopped in other logs, Auto-tune also tries switching off the emulator's multi-block translation after its earlier attempt.
- **Counter-Strike 2:** the sound broke up in every pass (fixed, see the sound fix below). The Dock start also ended at Steam's "update required" (error 19) without a word: the starting screen and Auto-tune now say that the game needs an update and to install it from its page. A Dock session that never drew a frame is also no longer counted as played, which lets Auto-tune's start rules fire for it.
- **DmC: Devil May Cry:** two logs met the Mono case described below (the check now runs by default). Its other stop, the engine's own `abort()` after 28 seconds with an empty log mirror, is not fixed: its recommended settings now mirror the engine's launch log so the next log names the error.
- **DOOM 3: BFG Edition:** a library entry whose program is `language_setup.exe` (a Qt language chooser that exits 0) looked like a game that closed by itself. The folder scan no longer offers that program, and a setup or language tool that closes within 15 seconds with exit code 0 and no picture now gets a note: "It looks like a setup or language tool, not the game. Add the game's own program from the same folder." Fixed.
- **Dying Light:** on a prefix whose Valve client files BCD Dock does not know, the start could not work and said little. BCD Dock now stops with a message that names the unsupported file; **Settings › BCD Dock › Valve's client files › Replace client components** puts the supported client in place, keeping the old folder and the installed games (not tested on a device yet). The recommended settings also mirror the engine's own log, because one run ended itself through the Steam client library's crash handler after 24 seconds (cause not known), and an experiment for a borderless window smaller than the screen, `env.MADEIRA_DISPLAY_FOLLOW_BORDERLESS = 1`, is off by default.
- **FIFA 23:** about 22 seconds in, the encode thread of the Direct3D 11 layer died on `UpdateSubresource` of a staging buffer, which Direct3D 11 ignores. Such a call is ignored now, and the recommended settings use the source-built Direct3D 11 that carries the fix. Fixed; later start-up steps of the game are not known.
- **FINAL FANTASY VII (2013):** the Qt 4 launcher died because a 33-character font face name overflowed a 32-character field and the SDK's checked copy aborted the host thread. The name is cut to what fits. Fixed.
- **FTL: Faster Than Light and Peggle Deluxe:** both locked up at their start: the emulator's thread-creation lock was taken twice by the thread that held it, when their sound library changed memory protection. The lock lets its owner in again. Fixed. Peggle Deluxe has a second stop that Auto-tune names (a host store into a page just made read-only); Auto-tune's experiment for it makes the game's executable memory plain read/write.
- **Grand Theft Auto V (Legacy, Enhanced and the Epic copy):**
  - the Epic copy of Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced starts Windows services with a native ARM64 program (`services.exe`) whose first emulator hook crashed on a thread with no emulator area; the hooks now leave such a thread alone, so the launcher can reach its service manager (not tested; a second stop in that program's first exception handling is named, not fixed);
  - the Grand Theft Auto V Legacy launcher's child program crashed in the emulator's allocation watch before its thread storage existed; that function now returns early when nothing is watched;
  - when the emulator's pooled memory ran out (Enhanced, 339 seconds in), it wrote through a NULL buffer on four threads at once; it now takes back idle buffers first, retries, and then refuses the allocation cleanly, so the game gets an error at its own address instead of a wedged emulator;
  - Social Club's browser helper could end BCD in a stale-pointer repair after a library was unmapped; that read is now checked;
  - the Launcher can say Steam is not running (error 113) although it is: this build logs a replica of the Launcher's own check so the next log names the failing step (Auto-tune says so), and a library entry without Steam can turn on the Windows services with `env.MADEIRA_ROCKSTAR_LOCAL_SERVICES = 1` (off by default).
- **Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX:** its launcher creates a Direct3D 12 bundle allocator, BCD answered "not implemented", and the launcher called through the NULL it got. Bundles now work: a bundle's commands are copied into the list that executes it. Fixed.
- **Maneater:** BCD's own fault handler died on a wild return address while it was only writing a log line, which ended the game after about 45 seconds with no message. Those reads are now checked. Fixed; what the game does next is not known.
- **Mass Effect: Legendary Edition and Selaco:** the emulator's own fault at process exit (its memory hooks used a context that was already gone) was filed as the end of the run and hid the real reason (Steam's ticket, no running Steam, a GPU-bound stall). The hooks now stand down once the process is terminating. Fixed.
- **Meccha Chameleon:** the Dock session never ended after the game's abort (exit code 3). That ends the session now. Fixed. Its Unreal loading thread also calls COM without an apartment and crashes; Auto-tune can add a rebuilt `combase` that creates the implicit apartment (not tested).

With the check off, 35 of the 36 archived sessions that met the case hung or crashed; with it on, Cult of the Lamb, Risk of Rain 2, Flotsam, Valheim and Probably Stolen ran.   - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_KEEP_ALIVE` (hold the session while a game's programs run).
  - `env.MADEIRA_ROCKSTAR_LOCAL_SERVICES`.
- **Diagnostics:** `env.MADEIRA_TLS_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_SEAM_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_FAULT_PEEK`, `env.MADEIRA_SPIN_DUMP_REGS`, `env.MADEIRA_STUCK_WAIT_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP`, `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_FAIL_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_OBJ_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_DIALOG_CODE_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_NVAPI_DEVICE_ID`.
- **More Windows DLLs that a game can ask for** in `env.MADEIRA_OPTIN_DLLS`: `msvcp_win`, `bluetoothapis`, `gameinput`, `ntdsapi`, `mfplay`, `avicap32`, `coremessaging`, `combase`, `dxdiagn`. Auto-tune can now add a second DLL to one it kept.
- **On by default, with a switch to turn them off:**
  - Each of these is a fix; `0` restores the old behaviour.
  - `env.MADEIRA_MZ_VIEW_CHECK`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_CLEAR_OWN_PROCESS`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_INDEX_SYNC`, `env.MADEIRA_UBI_CEF`, `env.MADEIRA_DESKTOP_CLOSE`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_REPAIR`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_CREATE`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_STEAM_VIEWS`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_CEG_SERVICE_RESTART`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_INSTALLERMESSAGE_PROVIDED`, `env.MADEIRA_PARADOX_LAUNCHER_MSI`, `env.MADEIRA_DIR_STORM`.
- 100 new host checks.

**Known issues:**
- External drives need BCD installed under its own identity: SideStore or AltStore, or a certificate signer with the bundle id changed to the certificate's App ID. Inside LiveContainer, or signed with a certificate that keeps BCD's original bundle id, iOS does not hand the chosen folder to BCD and **Open** in the folder picker does nothing. This is an iOS limit. Use exFAT or APFS; NTFS drives are read-only on iPhone and iPad.
- Red Dead Redemption 2 needs about 9.5 GB of RAM in play. Devices with 8 GB of RAM cannot hold it yet.
- GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Steam: the Rockstar Launcher sometimes says Steam is not running (error 113, "please reinstall") although it is. Fully close BCD and start the game again. This build logs what the launcher sees, to find the cause.
- Very long GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 sessions can stop when the emulator's memory area is full. Fully close BCD (swipe it away) and start again.
- Enshrouded and Hades II stop with a Steam "version mismatch": their Steam library is newer than the Steam client BCD Dock runs.
- The foldable iPhone's tabletop pose is in the code, but this build cannot read the hinge yet (it needs a newer iOS SDK).
- Windows Vulkan is new and tried on few games.

**Thanks** to @rbarton124, @pauloec, @iqui27, @creeper4004 and @Taala2 for their contributions to this release, and to Mila (mudcatpot) for the new icon.

Install help, game reports and ideas: join the [BCD-Games Discord](https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug).

**BCD.ipa**: the unsigned IPA, for sideloading with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. It needs iOS 18 or later and JIT; the README has the details.
**BCD-source.tar.xz**: the complete source of this build with all its submodules (GPL-3.0).

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

This build brings everything since 0.1.634: external drives, Windows Vulkan for 64-bit games (experimental, per game), Ubisoft Connect with Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4, a native interface for the foldable iPhone (experimental), colour profiles, many Direct3D 9, 11 and 12 fixes, Steam (BCD Dock) fixes, recommended settings for 60 more games and over 150 new Auto-tune rules.

## New

- **New icon:** BCD has a new app icon by Mila (mudcatpot), with versions for iOS's dark and tinted home screens. Thank you, Mila!
- **External drives:** **Settings › Storage › External drives › Add a drive or folder** adds a drive (a USB-C SSD or a stick) or a folder on it; you can add several. Each drive appears in Windows as `C:\External\<name>` and as a drive letter.
  - **Find games** adds the games on a drive to your library, and the drive's Steam libraries are found by themselves: their games start through BCD Dock like any other Steam game.
  - A Steam game's page offers **External drive** for a new install (**Steam installs** in the same settings picks the default place), and Steam updates and repairs a game in the library it lives in.
  - **Location › Move to** on a game's page moves a Steam game, or a game you added from Files, between the device and a drive: it copies the game, checks the copy, then deletes the original. The game keeps its settings, Workshop items and launch options.
  - Before a download, files already on the disk are checked once, so a repaired or moved game is not downloaded again.
  - The earlier External SSD folder becomes a drive by itself, with its games and their settings. If it does not open at the first start, BCD tries again at the next start or at Play.
  - **Reconnect** opens a drive again after it was unplugged; **Remove** forgets it.
- **Windows Vulkan (experimental, 64-bit games):** a game's page has **Direct3D › Vulkan (experimental)**. With it, a 64-bit game that draws with Vulkan gets Vulkan through MoltenVK (`vulkan = moltenvk`). Off by default; turn it on per game.
- **Ubisoft Connect, Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4:**
  - Ubisoft Connect no longer stops right after its start.
  - Its built-in browser runs with fewer processes, so it fits.
  - Its installer is not run again for every Ubisoft game once the launcher is installed.
  - A game started through it gets the settings the launcher needs for that session only.
  - Far Cry 3 and Far Cry 4 have recommended settings.
- **Foldable iPhone (experimental):** **Settings › Graphics › Foldable iPhone** has two switches, both off by default and both changing nothing on other iPhones and iPads.
  - **Duo enhancements** gives BCD a native interface with Liquid Glass, system tabs and a sidebar, search in the Library and controller navigation. The Windows desktop's Start, Open and Stop sit on Home, and downloads resume when the desktop runs in the background.
  - **Foldable iPhone support** starts a game you add at a resolution shaped like the inner display, and the touch controls follow the screen when you fold or unfold the phone.
  - Installed directly, iOS shows BCD in a small window on the inner display; inside LiveContainer it fills the screen. Both switches apply from the next start of BCD.
- **Colour profiles:** **Settings › Appearance** picks BCD's colours. The default look is unchanged.
- **Xbox 360 controller identity:** **Controls › Controller API › Xbox 360 controller (XInput + device)** on a game's page keeps the XInput pad and also lists it as an Xbox 360 controller, for a game that shows no controller otherwise (Far Cry 4).
- **Aim with a stick:** an aim zone can drive the right stick instead of the mouse (**Aim mode › The finger moves › The right stick** on a game's page), for a game that ignores the mouse while a controller is in use (NieR).

## Fixes and improvements

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** A game keeps the settings it had until you reset them. On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**, then check that **Options › Auto-tune › Auto-tune this game** is on, and start the game again.

Each fix targets the error a log showed; a game may now get further and still stop at a later point. If it does, please send a new log: it names the next problem.

### Games

Every game a log, a report or a test reached since 0.1.634. Where a game is not fixed, its line says which stop it passes now or which stop is named, and where it stops next when a log shows that.

#### Fixed in code

The stop the log showed cannot happen the same way any more. Almost none of these could be tried on a device yet, so a game may now get further and stop at a later point; where a log shows where that is, it is said.

- **1000xRESIST:** the Unity IL2CPP garbage collector raced with the game and ended it after 14 to 15 repairs of the same three virtual calls, about 16 seconds in at 54 FPS (the earlier frame-context experiment did not help). The repair has a fourth pass now that takes the object's class word and proves the table before it writes; and the recommended settings make the collector really suspend the game's threads (as for Megabonk, Big Walk, BALL x PIT and Lonely Mountains). Fixed for that fault; not tested on a device yet.
- **Age of Wonders 4:** the game asked Metal for a multisampled view of a single-sample texture and Metal's validation ended the game. The view now takes the texture's own type. Fixed.
- **Alan Wake:** about 67 Direct3D 9 pipelines per run were refused by the graphics driver, because a vertex shader that writes the point size was used in triangle draws; those draws were missing. The point size is now written only in point draws. Fixed. Text in a sent log's comment also no longer counts as the game's own log lines (it had produced a false "known stop"). For the crash at the end of a run, where BCD itself ended while a game thread exited, two experiments exist for the game's own settings, off by default: `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_DIAG = 1` names the object and `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP = 1` skips that clean-up.
- **Assassin's Creed (2007):** it died after Steam's helper program unloaded and cleared the game's thread-local data. A program's `TlsFree` now clears slots only in its own program's threads, as on Windows (`env.MADEIRA_TLS_CLEAR_OWN_PROCESS = 0` brings the old behaviour back). Fixed.
- **Battlefield 2 and Cold Fear:** the shader converter did not know the compressed-normal vertex formats DEC3N and UDEC3 and stopped the game, Battlefield 2 about 40 seconds in and Cold Fear at its first 3D scene. Both formats are converted now. Fixed. Battlefield 2 with a Direct3D wrapper in its folder can also stop on a stale memory alias; Auto-tune now tries the setting that releases stale memory aliases for it.
- **BioShock:** the game stopped about 110 seconds after the logos, when its renderer thread read a NULL getter right after the first run-time HLSL compiles. Wine's D3DX compile functions never wrote the result variable (`pHResult`) that the game passes; the six functions now write it as Windows documents. This is the likely cause, not proved; if it still stops, the log now holds the compiler's text for every failed compile (24 per process, with the first 160 bytes of the source). The recommended settings keep a file trace of 20,000 lines so the name of the shader-error file shows. For "no sound after the intro", `env.MADEIRA_AUDIO_CAPTURE = 1` (off by default; put it in the game's own settings) offers one silent recording device, never the microphone and never mixed.
- **Black Mesa:** its own crash handler closes the game with exit code 1 after 17 seconds, and the BCD Dock session stayed open on a dead picture. A game that closes within 30 seconds without a picture now ends its session, whatever its exit code. Fixed. The crash itself (a call from Qt's QML engine into an empty page) is not fixed; the log now says whether BCD's views of that page agree.
- **Blur:** the game's protected start-up code uses an x86 bit-scan with a redundant prefix that the emulator rejected ("Invalid instruction"). That form and a few similar ones now decode. Fixed; the stub may stop at its next instruction.
- **Bulletstorm, Hitman: Blood Money, Medal of Honor: Airborne and LEGO Marvel Super Heroes** (BCD Dock): the 32-bit game said Steam was not running (error 113, "Problem starting up Steam") because the Dock wrote Steam's entries only where 64-bit programs read them. They are now also written where a 32-bit game reads them (an entry of a client that is gone is overwritten for the session). Fixed. Bulletstorm's recommended settings also dump the registers at its start-up fault; started directly, Hitman: Blood Money shows "Failed to find Steam", which Auto-tune now answers with "start it with BCD Dock".
- **Capcom games** (Resident Evil 3, Resident Evil 4, Resident Evil Requiem, Monster Hunter Rise, Monster Hunter Stories 3 trial, Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection, Onimusha): their first start ran only Capcom's codec notice, a .NET program that cannot run under Wine Mono and installs nothing, then asked you to restart BCD. BCD now treats that notice as provided, so the first Play starts the game. Fixed. For Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection and Monster Hunter Rise, whose packed program then stopped in other logs, Auto-tune also tries switching off the emulator's multi-block translation after its earlier attempt.
- **Counter-Strike 2:** the sound broke up in every pass (fixed, see the sound fix below). The Dock start also ended at Steam's "update required" (error 19) without a word: the starting screen and Auto-tune now say that the game needs an update and to install it from its page. A Dock session that never drew a frame is also no longer counted as played, which lets Auto-tune's start rules fire for it.
- **DmC: Devil May Cry:** two logs met the Mono case described below (the check now runs by default). Its other stop, the engine's own `abort()` after 28 seconds with an empty log mirror, is not fixed: its recommended settings now mirror the engine's launch log so the next log names the error.
- **DOOM 3: BFG Edition:** a library entry whose program is `language_setup.exe` (a Qt language chooser that exits 0) looked like a game that closed by itself. The folder scan no longer offers that program, and a setup or language tool that closes within 15 seconds with exit code 0 and no picture now gets a note: "It looks like a setup or language tool, not the game. Add the game's own program from the same folder." Fixed.
- **Dying Light:** on a prefix whose Valve client files BCD Dock does not know, the start could not work and said little. BCD Dock now stops with a message that names the unsupported file; **Settings › BCD Dock › Valve's client files › Replace client components** puts the supported client in place, keeping the old folder and the installed games (not tested on a device yet). The recommended settings also mirror the engine's own log, because one run ended itself through the Steam client library's crash handler after 24 seconds (cause not known), and an experiment for a borderless window smaller than the screen, `env.MADEIRA_DISPLAY_FOLLOW_BORDERLESS = 1`, is off by default.
- **FIFA 23:** about 22 seconds in, the encode thread of the Direct3D 11 layer died on `UpdateSubresource` of a staging buffer, which Direct3D 11 ignores. Such a call is ignored now, and the recommended settings use the source-built Direct3D 11 that carries the fix. Fixed; later start-up steps of the game are not known.
- **FINAL FANTASY VII (2013):** the Qt 4 launcher died because a 33-character font face name overflowed a 32-character field and the SDK's checked copy aborted the host thread. The name is cut to what fits. Fixed.
- **FTL: Faster Than Light and Peggle Deluxe:** both locked up at their start: the emulator's thread-creation lock was taken twice by the thread that held it, when their sound library changed memory protection. The lock lets its owner in again. Fixed. Peggle Deluxe has a second stop that Auto-tune names (a host store into a page just made read-only); Auto-tune's experiment for it makes the game's executable memory plain read/write.
- **Grand Theft Auto V (Legacy, Enhanced and the Epic copy):**
  - the Epic copy of Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced starts Windows services with a native ARM64 program (`services.exe`) whose first emulator hook crashed on a thread with no emulator area; the hooks now leave such a thread alone, so the launcher can reach its service manager (not tested; a second stop in that program's first exception handling is named, not fixed);
  - the Grand Theft Auto V Legacy launcher's child program crashed in the emulator's allocation watch before its thread storage existed; that function now returns early when nothing is watched;
  - when the emulator's pooled memory ran out (Enhanced, 339 seconds in), it wrote through a NULL buffer on four threads at once; it now takes back idle buffers first, retries, and then refuses the allocation cleanly, so the game gets an error at its own address instead of a wedged emulator;
  - Social Club's browser helper could end BCD in a stale-pointer repair after a library was unmapped; that read is now checked;
  - the Launcher can say Steam is not running (error 113) although it is: this build logs a replica of the Launcher's own check so the next log names the failing step (Auto-tune says so), and a library entry without Steam can turn on the Windows services with `env.MADEIRA_ROCKSTAR_LOCAL_SERVICES = 1` (off by default).
- **Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX:** its launcher creates a Direct3D 12 bundle allocator, BCD answered "not implemented", and the launcher called through the NULL it got. Bundles now work: a bundle's commands are copied into the list that executes it. Fixed.
- **Maneater:** BCD's own fault handler died on a wild return address while it was only writing a log line, which ended the game after about 45 seconds with no message. Those reads are now checked. Fixed; what the game does next is not known.
- **Mass Effect: Legendary Edition and Selaco:** the emulator's own fault at process exit (its memory hooks used a context that was already gone) was filed as the end of the run and hid the real reason (Steam's ticket, no running Steam, a GPU-bound stall). The hooks now stand down once the process is terminating. Fixed.
- **Meccha Chameleon:** the Dock session never ended after the game's abort (exit code 3). That ends the session now. Fixed. Its Unreal loading thread also calls COM without an apartment and crashes; Auto-tune can add a rebuilt `combase` that creates the implicit apartment (not tested).
- **Mono and Unity games** that hung or crashed because a Mono code chunk started in the slack behind a mapped .NET assembly: the check for that case is now on by default (`env.MADEIRA_MZ_VIEW_CHECK = 0` restores the old handling). With the check off, 35 of the 36 archived sessions that met the case hung or crashed; with it on, Cult of the Lamb, Risk of Rain 2, Flotsam, Valheim and Probably Stolen ran. Fixed for Hollow Knight, Hollow Knight: Silksong, ULTRAKILL, Subnautica: Below Zero, FEZ, Owlboy, Graveyard Keeper 2, Thief Simulator 3, Universe Sandbox, SpeedRunners 2, Another Crab's Treasure, CloverPit, Sorry We're Closed, TerraTech and Wizard with a Gun, and possibly for Happy's Humble Burger Farm (it hung when started from the library and played from the Windows desktop). Probably Stolen, on a first Dock start without a network connection, is now told to connect once (no saved sign-in).
- **Need for Speed: Underground:** a page that the emulator promoted, freed and reused with data execution prevention off was never promoted again and ended in "no execute". It is promoted again. Fixed.
- **NTE: Neverness to Everness and Dominus Gladiatus:** the emulator's allocation of a 16 MB (and, for Dominus Gladiatus, 8 MB) code-translation buffer failed, and it wrote at address 0x800010 holding a lock that wedged every other thread. It now takes back idle pooled buffers first, then retries, then refuses the allocation cleanly, so the game gets a fault at its own address. Fixed; if its memory is truly full the session usually still ends, now without a wild write.
- **PRAGMATA:** like the other Capcom games above, its first Play ran only Capcom's codec notice and now starts the game. The program then reads a wild pointer in its first second; its recommended settings add the protected-code experiment (registers that only look like shared-page pointers are left alone), which should pass that first second if the guess is right.
- **Prison Architect and Hearts of Iron IV** (and the other Paradox games started through `dowser.exe`): the launcher stub could not find `msiexec`, and its installer failed on a missing `Msi.dll`. The Dock now gives the launcher Windows Installer. Fixed for those two steps; the launcher may stop at a later wall. Hearts of Iron IV's recommended settings also list the same files.
- **Quake II, Resonance, Counter-Strike 2, Deadlock, Dead Rising, Murder Miners, MARVEL Cosmic Invasion, Mina the Hollower, Story of Seasons, Metal Gear Solid 2, Jazzpunk, Need for Speed: The Run, skate and NW.js games** (about 20 games, 40 logs; Metal Gear Solid 2's launcher also hung on build 634, which is likely the Mono case above): the sound broke up because the game queues two 10 ms periods while iOS pulls about 21 ms, so every pass had a gap. When a stream comes up short in nearly every pass for 20 seconds, BCD now asks iOS once per run for a 5 ms audio buffer, as `env.MADEIRA_AUDIO_IO_MS = 5` does; other games are not touched. Fixed for the logs it came from; not tested on a device yet. Quake II and Resonance carry that line in their recommended settings. Resonance's controller (DualSense in HID mode) also logs a one-minute line of what the game reads, and Quake II's file and registry trace names what the engine looks up before it chooses Direct3D 11 over Vulkan.
- **REANIMAL and Oar'some Adventures:** Metal aborted on a 64-bit texture atomic on A15, M1 and M2 chips, because the game was told the GPU had it. 64-bit texture atomics are now used only where the GPU has them (Apple9 and later). Fixed. REANIMAL's recommended settings also report capabilities by GPU family, so the game stops using the feature.
- **Red Dead Redemption 2:** Metal aborted on a 64-bit texture atomic on M1 chips (see REANIMAL above), which is fixed. Also new: a notice for a program started from the Windows desktop that has recommended settings (they apply only when it is added as a game with the + button), Auto-tune words for a start without the launcher ("choose the launcher's program"), and for the Launcher's Steam error 113 the replica line named under Grand Theft Auto V.
- **Resident Evil 5 and Portal:** a 32-bit program stored an uninitialised status block over translated code on phones with the small address map and ended with an illegal instruction. A status block that lies in a pool copy's code is now skipped. Fixed. For Resident Evil 5, a copy that carries its own `winmm.dll` now uses BCD's through the recommended settings, and the protection exit of the Steam copy (exit code `0x5...`) is named by Auto-tune and dumped with the 32-bit fault dump.
- **Rise of the Tomb Raider, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, The Witness, Transformers and Danganronpa:** a texture of an impossible size (an edge above 16384, or 32768 on the newest GPUs; a 3D texture or array above 2048) made Metal abort the game. Direct3D 12 and Direct3D 11 now refuse it with the error Windows gives, and a native check refuses it before Metal sees it. Fixed for the abort; the game may still fail later. A 64-bit Direct3D 11 game gets the Direct3D 11 part through the source-built Direct3D 11 (`env.MADEIRA_D3D11_SRC = 1`).
- **Roommate (demo) and The Edge Of: Definitive Edition:** a damaged relocation table of the program image sent BCD's loop outside the image: Roommate ended BCD with a bad store, The Edge Of hung for 57 to 76 seconds holding BCD's memory lock. The three walks now check every block and entry against the image. Fixed.
- **S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky:** after the earlier `point` fix, the game stopped on "Reservation shader target ps": the HLSL compiler turned `register(ps, c0)` into an error. A reservation that names a shader target now applies when compiling for it and is ignored for others, as Direct3D's compiler does. Fixed. Six more Direct3D 9 words are read as names, and a refused shader's source can be dumped with `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_FAIL_DUMP = 1` (off) if the next wall is another shader. The Shadow of Chernobyl and Call of Pripyat versions share the compiler.
- **Satisfactory and Subnautica 2:** Unreal Engine's Direct3D 12 renderer stopped at its first texture upload on "Footprint.Width % BlockSizeX == 0": copy footprints of block-compressed textures must come in whole blocks, as Windows reports them. They do now (a copy that overruns the mip is clipped). Fixed; `d3d12-footprint-block-align = 0` turns the change off. Unreal's media library `mfplay` is missing from the 64-bit set; Auto-tune can add Wine's.
- **Slay the Spire 2:** the game did not start when the translation pool's placement left no room for the 0x140000000 executable window ("BAD POOL placement"); BCD now retries with a pool smaller by 16 MB steps when that window is held. Fixed for that stop. Its recommended settings also keep the pool clear of the window. The game's other crash (a .NET code stub across a pool seam) is not fixed: the experiments for it, `env.MADEIRA_SEAM_TRACE = 1` (names the seams) and `env.MADEIRA_ANON_POOL_ADJACENT = 1`, are off by default.
- **Slime Rancher 2:** in a windowed game BCD mapped every tap, click and pointer position to the whole screen while the picture shown is the game's window, so a 1158x832 window in the middle of the screen took no click. They now land in the window. Fixed. Its recommended settings also give the game Wine's `wintypes.dll` (for the "Failed to load il2cpp" stop) and publish controllers through Windows.Gaming.Input (not tested with this game yet).
- **Splinter Cell: Conviction:** at a thread's exit the emulator kept a pointer to a destroyed thread state, and a second fault read through it. The pointer is now cleared after the state is destroyed. Fixed for that fault; the game also hangs for 60 seconds at its start (it waits for events nobody sets) and a part of the thread exit inside BCD is not changed yet.
- **Terraria, Stardew Valley, Team Fortress 2 and Grind Survivors** (BCD Dock): Steam's host answered result 42 because the machine key `HKLM\Software\Valve\Steam` was missing. BCD now puts missing Steam client entries back before each Dock start, and the host creates the key when it is absent. Fixed. For Grind Survivors a normal quit was also reported as a crash because the emulator's memory hooks faulted at exit; they now stand down once the process is terminating. Fixed. Unreal's media library `mfplay` can be added by Auto-tune for it.
- **The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and Repentance+:** a game that died with an unusual exit status within 30 seconds left the Dock session open on a black window; any short exit without a picture now ends the session. Fixed. The 32-bit game also gets a 1 GB Lua reservation outside its 4 GB window and stops: its recommended settings dump the code, registers and stack at that fault, and `env.MADEIRA_WOW_JUMBO_INSIDE = 1` (off) refuses such a reservation with "no memory" as an experiment. With OpenGL ES chosen on its page it stops on a NULL `glClear`; Auto-tune now says to choose another OpenGL backend. Repentance+ comes up on Zink and then its own loop spins at 100 % on four threads: the log now shows the code around the hottest address.
- **The Escapists and Psych Engine:** the Epic start of The Escapists and Psych Engine's "open releases page" both run `cmd.exe /c start ...` as a native ARM64 child, whose first emulator hook crashed (the same defect as Grand Theft Auto V's service program above). The hooks leave such a thread alone. Fixed; Psych Engine's own NULL read 60 seconds later is not explained, and its first Lua script ends the game because a LuaJIT built into the exe needs memory below 2 GB (Auto-tune names it; no setting is known).

#### New or changed recommended settings

Use **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended** on a game's page to get its new settings. None of these rows could be tried on a device yet unless it says so, and a game may now get further and stop at a later point.

- **Angry Birds:** Rovio's PC build (32-bit, OpenGL only) said "OpenGL 2.0 renderer not supported" against BCD's no-OpenGL stub and ended after 13 seconds. Its recommended settings now turn on BCD's own OpenGL (Zink). A 32-bit game on a phone with 2.3 GB is the hard case; the other choice is OpenGL ES.
- **Arctic Drive Demo:** the first start failed without Wine's `wintypes.dll`; Auto-tune kept the line that links Wine's `wintypes.dll` and the next start played for 36 minutes, so the recommended settings now carry the line from the first start. That session then ended after one recovered GPU error because iOS killed the app at 99.4 % of its memory limit: Auto-tune now scores it as a memory kill (it had scored it as a hang), and its block-compressed textures (23 % of the limit) make the mip clamp the first attempt. Another log ended when the emulator's pool ran out (UE5, 49 seconds in); the allocation is now refused cleanly instead of written through NULL.
- **Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced:** the 478 MB program does not fit the translation pool, so its recommended settings run it from the loaded image; the loader then stopped on `GameInput.dll`, which the 64-bit set lacked, and BCD now ships Wine's GameInput stub for a game that lists it. What the game does next is not known.
- **Baba Is You:** Wine's Direct3D 9 needs OpenGL, which BCD does not have, and the game's DXVK fallback needs Vulkan, so the game ended after 2 seconds. Its recommended settings give it DXMT's Direct3D 9. If it then asks for something else, Windows Vulkan (**Direct3D › Vulkan (experimental)**) is the next experiment.
- **Battlefield 1942** (and the mods that use its program, such as Desert Combat): Wine's Direct3D 8 found no OpenGL, the game wrote "Failed to init Direct3D" and exited with 0x31. Its recommended settings run Direct3D 8 on Direct3D 9.
- **BlueField:** the Unreal Engine 5 fan game's shipping program imports `tbs.dll`, which the 64-bit set lacks; its recommended settings add Wine's `tbs` as an opt-in DLL. What it does after its imports is not known.

- **Just Cause 3:** the world load ran 8.4 seconds in one GPU command buffer at 14 FPS (tessellated draws are suspected). One slow frame is traced now, not three in a row.
- **Look Outside:** BCD's own Swift thread used 94 % of a core; the log now prints that thread's call chain once.
- **Mafia II (Classic), Bionic Commando, Spec Ops: The Line, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Saints Row, Just Cause 2, XCOM: Enemy Unknown, Kane & Lynch 2, Sid Meier's Civilization V and Duke Nukem Forever:** the CEG job that Steam runs at their start never finished or came back with result 55 or 3. BCD Dock now starts Steam's client service again (up to 3 times) if it died after its 2-second settle, the log shows the service's own log, the connection and why the job failed, the starting screen says it is still preparing, and Auto-tune names each result. No fix is claimed.
- **MakeRoom:** the log now prints the first audible buffer of every stream and the endpoint's state, to tell a silent game from a stopped or muted device.
- **Mount & Blade: Warband and LEGO Batman 2:** a late 32-bit crash through a wild pointer now gets the fault dump offer from Auto-tune up to stage 5, so the first log of such a crash carries it.
- **Need for Speed: SHIFT:** the game played 20 seconds at 57 FPS, then read NULL at `shift.exe+0x432056` after a Direct3D 9 or DirectInput call answered "not implemented". Its recommended settings add the 32-bit fault dump and DXMT's ring of the last 64 Direct3D 9 calls, so the next log names the call.
- **R.E.P.O. and GeoGuessr: Steam Edition** (BCD Dock): Valve's launch refusals are now named on the starting screen (33: the game may be refused by Family Sharing; 45: choose another launch option) and the launch entry's fields are logged.
- **Requiem: Avenging Angel:** the 32-bit Glide-wrapper game shows black UI rectangles. The GPU trace frame moves from 20 s to 14 s (it had fallen on a loading screen, not the menu), and `UnlockRect` pixel statistics print under `DXMT_DUMP_D9_SHADER`.
- **Ryse: Son of Rome:** BCD itself crashed once in 3,600 logs when a WoW64 thread's stack had been released. The log now keeps a ring of the last TEB frees and names which block the crashing address belongs to.
- **Sekiro:** iOS reports GPU stalls of 10 to 33 seconds with no guilty buffer. A `[gpu-error]` line now gives victim and culprit, thermal state and timing.
- **Subnautica:** the wide report for an impossible instruction pointer now prints the slot that the producing load read and its neighbours, to show whether the stored word is torn (the earlier experiment, `env.MADEIRA_CTX_FRAME`, did not help).
- **Surviving Mars:** the text of a 64-bit program's message boxes was missing in the log; the text of a box's static and button children is printed now.
- **SWAT Commander: Prologue:** next to each memory burst the log now prints Metal's allocated size, to separate GPU growth from guest memory.
- **The Amazing Spider-Man (2012):** Auto-tune's shader rule had told players "a crash in BCD itself" for a crash in the game's own worker thread (a call through NULL). The rule now speaks only for a session that played, and the crash gets the fault dump.
- **The Witcher 2:** the launcher ends with status 0 at once and no picture is drawn (the real program is `bin\witcher2.exe`). Its recommended settings add a file trace (40,000 lines, because Steam's client uses the default budget first) and a registry trace.
- **Wolfpack:** the 64-bit Unity game with its own `mono.dll` plays slowly (12.5 million emulated stores in 98 seconds); the log now lists large read/write/execute views so the next log shows what they are. `env.MADEIRA_GUEST_RWX_DATA = 2` (off) treats views of 4 MB and more as data.
- **Yakuza: Like a Dragon:** the protected program jumps into the middle of an instruction after a nested split atomic. Its illegal-instruction report now carries the x86 register set, and Auto-tune names the stop.

#### Checked, no failure in the log

Feeding Frenzy and Left 4 Dead 2: the logs showed no failure (the game ran, or the player left), so nothing changed.

#### Reviewed, outside BCD's scope

Call of Duty HQ, EA SPORTS FC 26, Horizon Walker and My Hero Ultra Rumble: their own protection or anti-cheat ended them.

### Graphics

- **Direct3D 9:**
  - The vertex formats DEC3N and UDEC3 (compressed normals and tangents) work. They stopped Battlefield 2 about 40 seconds in and Cold Fear at its first 3D scene.
  - A vertex shader that writes the point size works in triangle and line draws. Alan Wake lost many of its pipelines this way.
- **Direct3D 11:**
  - `UpdateSubresource` on a staging buffer is ignored as on Windows (FIFA 23 stopped).
  - The swap chain answers `SetRotation` and `GetRotation`, so SDL2 games start (The Battle for Wesnoth).
  - A texture larger than Direct3D 11 allows is refused with an error the game can handle, instead of ending it (The Witness, Rise of the Tomb Raider, Transformers, Danganronpa).
- **Direct3D 12:**
  - Command bundles work (Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX's launcher).
  - Copy footprints of block-compressed textures come in whole blocks, as Windows reports them (Satisfactory and other Unreal Engine 5 games stopped at their first texture upload).
  - 64-bit texture atomics are used only on GPUs that have them; on A15, M1 and M2 the game no longer stops (REANIMAL).
  - A texture view of the other sample count, and a texture larger than the GPU allows, no longer end the game (Age of Wonders 4, Shadow of the Tomb Raider).
  - Fences answer `ID3D12Fence1` and heaps answer `ID3D12Heap1`, as on Windows; a game that created its fences or heaps through these interfaces took the refusal for an error (one showed "not enough system and video memory" at its start).
  - Resources, heaps, descriptor heaps, query heaps, fences, pipeline states, command allocators, command signatures and command queues answer `ID3D12Pageable`.
  - Shaders that read the result of a 64-bit texture atomic are converted.
  - A clear of a texture to zero through a view of another texel size is done, not skipped.
  - Many clear values in one frame are written exactly.
  - A shader the converter refuses is named in the log with the converter's message.
  - With the pipeline library switch on (`d3d12-pipeline-library = 1`), the shader cache capability also reports pipeline libraries.
- **Metal limits:** a texture larger than every Apple GPU supports is refused before Metal sees it, so the game gets an error instead of being ended.
- **HLSL compiler (shaders compiled while the game runs):**
  - `register(ps, c0)` and similar forms are accepted (S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky).
  - Six more Direct3D 9 words are read as names.
  - The Direct3D 10/11 compile helpers report their result as Windows does.
- **NVAPI** (with **Report an NVIDIA GPU** on): calls made with a null GPU handle now answer for the first GPU, as NVIDIA's driver does.
- **OpenGL:** auto-tune recognises more OpenGL-only games and turns BCD's OpenGL on for them (DOOM 64, Deponia, Into the Breach, Angry Birds, AppGameKit and Godot 4 games).

### Steam (BCD Dock)

- **"Steam is not running" (error 113) in 32-bit games:** Steam's entries are now also written where a 32-bit game reads them (Hitman: Blood Money, Bulletstorm, Medal of Honor: Airborne, LEGO Marvel Super Heroes).
- **Error 42 at the start:** missing Steam client entries are put back before each start (Terraria, Stardew Valley, Team Fortress 2, Grind Survivors).
- **A game that closes on its own** within 30 seconds without a picture now ends its session, whatever code it ends with (Black Mesa, The Binding of Isaac, Meccha Chameleon). Before, you had to close it yourself.
- **A starter that closes before its game** no longer takes Steam away from the game (Control).
- **Unsupported Steam client files:** Valve client files BCD Dock does not support are named. **Settings › BCD Dock › Valve's client files › Replace client components** puts supported ones in place; nothing is deleted.
- **Steam's refusals named:** "update required" (error 19) and "playing on another device" (error 35) are named on the starting screen and by auto-tune.
- **Copy protection (CEG):** the Steam client service is started again when it stops, and the log shows why a CEG job failed.
- **Install scripts:** Capcom's codec notice is no longer run (every Capcom game's first start only ran installs). The Paradox launcher gets Windows Installer (Prison Architect, Hearts of Iron IV).

### The app

- **JIT memory:** when StikDebug has been attached for a while or the phone is hot, the starting screen says before the request that the screen can freeze for up to 30 seconds. After 30 seconds without an answer it says how to start again. The box at the next start adds that StikDebug stops answering far more often on a hot phone.
- **Low Power Mode:** the starting screen says when it is on, because games and launchers then start and run much slower.
- **iPad:** a game's **Resolution** row says that a lower resolution (with MetalFX upscaling) is the first thing to try when a game stutters.
- **A game left in the background:** the crash box of a session that ran 90 seconds or more says to stay in BCD while the game runs, because iOS closes a large app that goes to the background.
- **Start over:** a game's page has **Start over with BCD's settings** under Recommended settings. A reset never touches the game's own files, saves or in-game options.
- **A copy that cannot run games:** a copy installed without the debugging right now shows "This copy can't run games yet" and the reason, instead of the setup pages.
- **Landscape lock:** a lock is applied again when BCD comes back from the background (a game showed in half the screen after returning).
- **Memory kills:** the text names the device's own memory limit and says when a game needs a device with more.

### Windows desktop

- **Close** and **Start › Shut Down** end the Windows desktop session.
- A program started from the desktop that has recommended settings gets a note that they apply when it is added as a game.

### Audio

- A game whose sound broke up in every frame (Quake II, Counter-Strike 2, Deadlock, Resonance, Dead Rising and others) gets a shorter audio buffer by itself.

### Memory and the emulator

- Thread contexts carry the vector registers, as on Windows.
- Two leaks of the emulator's code memory are closed.
- Each Windows module gets its own thread-local data slot (before, some shared the main program's).
- Freeing a thread-local slot no longer clears it in other programs of the session, as on Windows (Assassin's Creed).
- **No longer end the game or hang:**
  - Damaged relocation tables (Roommate, The Edge Of).
  - A 32-bit stack overflow, now reported as one.
  - A self-locking 32-bit start (FTL, Peggle Deluxe).
  - .NET services started from a 64-bit session (the Epic version of GTA V Enhanced, The Escapists).
  - Several x86 instruction forms with a REP prefix.
- Mono and Unity games whose code sits behind a .NET assembly no longer hang (the MZ view check is now on by default).
- A Unity game's garbage collector race is repaired in one more case (1000xRESIST).
- A crash inside BCD's own fault handling on a wild return address is gone (Maneater).
- Windowed games: taps, clicks and the pointer land in the game's window (Slime Rancher 2).

### Auto-tune

- A session that never drew a frame is no longer counted as played.
- A memory kill is recognised after a recovered GPU error.
- A game's block-compressed textures can trigger the texture size clamp before a swap file.
- A start where Wine never began is not scored.
- A player's own swap size is kept while the other swap lines are tried.
- A rule can say what to choose instead of "No setting changes this".
- Text written in a sent log's comment no longer counts as the game's.
- Over 150 new rules, among them those for the fixes above, 64-bit games that need an extra Windows DLL (Watch Dogs, DRAGON BALL FighterZ, Ghost of Tsushima, Momo Game, Football Manager 2020, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced), protected games that need their registers kept (Football Manager 2024 and 27, Yakuza Kiwami 3, PRAGMATA, Metaphor: ReFantazio), Direct3D 8 games, memory kills and many known stops.
- A build number like `634.4` (a re-signed copy) is read as 634, so recommended settings with a minimum build apply.

### Recommended settings

**New:** Angry Birds, Arctic Drive Demo, Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, Astro Tripper, Baba Is You, Battlefield 1942, BlueField, Brotato, Buckshot Roulette, Bulletstorm, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Call of Duty: World at War, Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy, Dark Deception: Chapter 1, Deponia: The Complete Journey, Dishonored, DmC: Devil May Cry, DOOM 64, DRAGON BALL FighterZ, Dying Light: The Beast, Eslabong, Far Cry 3 (outside Steam), Far Cry 4, FIFA 23, Fear & Hunger 2: Termina, Find The Needle Demo, Football Manager 2020, Football Manager (outside Steam), FreshWomen - Season 1, GP Bikes, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Half Sword Demo, Hearts of Iron IV, Inscryption, Into the Breach, Killer Instinct, L.A. Noire, Mafia, Metaphor: ReFantazio, Mirror's Edge, Momo Game, Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), Need for Speed: SHIFT, Noita, POLYBIUS, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown, Quake II, REPLACED, Resonance, SC Jogos (Barro GT), Slime Rancher 2, Sonic Generations, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, THE KING OF FIGHTERS XIV, The Witcher 2, Watch Dogs, Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties.

**Updated:** 1000xRESIST, Balatro, BioShock, Burnout Paradise: The Ultimate Box, Control, CrossCode, DARK SOULS III, DRAGON BALL: Sparking! ZERO, Dying Light, Fallout 3, Far Cry 3, Football Manager 27, Ghost of Tsushima, Halo: The Master Chief Collection, Hitman: Contracts, Just Cause 3, Max Payne 3, Mewgenics, Need for Speed: Underground 2, No More Room in Hell, Oxygen Not Included, PRAGMATA, Poppy Playtime, REANIMAL, Requiem: Avenging Angel, Resident Evil 5, Slay the Spire 2, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, Ubisoft Connect.

### Logs

- **Error box code dump:** with `env.MADEIRA_DIALOG_CODE_DUMP = 1` (off by default), the log shows the game's own code that showed an error box.
- New lines name more failures:
  - A program's damaged relocation table.
  - A 32-bit program's huge reservation.
  - Long directory listings.
  - Failed opens of named objects (on request).
  - A refused HLSL shader's source (on request).
  - The first audible sound of a game.
  - GPU errors with their timing.
  - Steam's view of a game's start (Steam client entries, the game's own Steam check).
  - The Steam client's connection while a CEG job waits.

### Under the hood

Everything below is off by default unless a game's recommended settings or auto-tune turn it on.

- **Direct3D 12:**
  - `d3d12-device9`, `d3d12-fence-flags` (shared fence flags).
  - `dxil-target-latest` (convert shaders for the device's newest GPU family).
  - `dxil-loop-guard` (stop listed shaders' loops after 65,536 rounds instead of hanging the GPU).
  - `heap-backing` mode 2.
  - `trace-buffer-size` and `trace-dispatch` (diagnostics).
  - `d3d12-footprint-block-align = 0` turns this build's footprint change off.
- **Direct3D 9 and 11:** `env.MADEIRA_VIEW_PRIVATE_REF`, `env.DXMT_MODE_LIST_ANY_BPP`.
- **Vulkan:** `vulkan`, `env.MADEIRA_VULKAN_LIBRARY`, `env.MADEIRA_VK_HOST_SUBOPTIMAL`.
- **OpenGL:** `env.MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, `env.MESA_GLSL_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, `env.MADEIRA_GL_EMPTY_EXTENSIONS`.
- **Memory:**
  - `env.MADEIRA_BIG_HINT_EXACT` (modes 2 and 3).
  - `env.MADEIRA_JUMBO_HALF = 2`, `oversize-reserve-min-mb`, `oversize-reserve-eager`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_FEX_ARENA_REAP`, `env.MADEIRA_WOW_JUMBO_INSIDE`, `env.MADEIRA_X64_RWX_PLAIN`, `env.MADEIRA_GUEST_RWX_DATA = 2`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_ANON_POOL_ADJACENT`, `env.MADEIRA_COMMIT_GUARD_CLEAR`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CARVE_MERGE`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_FOREGROUND`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_DEFER_FREE`, `env.MADEIRA_POOL_CODE_KEEP_BIG`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_X64_HOOK_ZONE`, `env.MADEIRA_SELF_WRITE`, `env.MADEIRA_KILL_REAP`.
- **Emulator and Wine:**
  - `env.MADEIRA_FEX_SPLIT_LOCK`, `env.FEX_SMCCHECKS`, `env.MADEIRA_CTX_FP`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_SLEEP_KERNEL_APC`, `env.MADEIRA_WOA_RECHECK`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DNS_REFUSE_CRASH` (do not contact Valve's crash-report server).
  - `env.MADEIRA_DISPLAY_FOLLOW_BORDERLESS`.
- **Audio:** `env.MADEIRA_AUDIO_CAPTURE` (one silent recording device, never the microphone).
- **Steam (BCD Dock):**
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_KEEP_ALIVE` (hold the session while a game's programs run).
  - `env.MADEIRA_ROCKSTAR_LOCAL_SERVICES`.
- **Diagnostics:** `env.MADEIRA_TLS_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_SEAM_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_FAULT_PEEK`, `env.MADEIRA_SPIN_DUMP_REGS`, `env.MADEIRA_STUCK_WAIT_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_DIAG`, `env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP`, `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_FAIL_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_OBJ_TRACE`, `env.MADEIRA_DIALOG_CODE_DUMP`, `env.MADEIRA_NVAPI_DEVICE_ID`.
- **More Windows DLLs that a game can ask for** in `env.MADEIRA_OPTIN_DLLS`: `msvcp_win`, `bluetoothapis`, `gameinput`, `ntdsapi`, `mfplay`, `avicap32`, `coremessaging`, `combase`, `dxdiagn`. Auto-tune can now add a second DLL to one it kept.
- **On by default, with a switch to turn them off:**
  - Each of these is a fix; `0` restores the old behaviour.
  - `env.MADEIRA_MZ_VIEW_CHECK`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_CLEAR_OWN_PROCESS`, `env.MADEIRA_TLS_INDEX_SYNC`, `env.MADEIRA_UBI_CEF`, `env.MADEIRA_DESKTOP_CLOSE`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_REPAIR`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_REGISTRY_CREATE`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_STEAM_VIEWS`, `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_CEG_SERVICE_RESTART`.
  - `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_INSTALLERMESSAGE_PROVIDED`, `env.MADEIRA_PARADOX_LAUNCHER_MSI`, `env.MADEIRA_DIR_STORM`.
- 100 new host checks.

**Known issues:**
- External drives need BCD installed under its own identity: SideStore or AltStore, or a certificate signer with the bundle id changed to the certificate's App ID. Inside LiveContainer, or signed with a certificate that keeps BCD's original bundle id, iOS does not hand the chosen folder to BCD and **Open** in the folder picker does nothing. This is an iOS limit. Use exFAT or APFS; NTFS drives are read-only on iPhone and iPad.
- Red Dead Redemption 2 needs about 9.5 GB of RAM in play. Devices with 8 GB of RAM cannot hold it yet.
- GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 from Steam: the Rockstar Launcher sometimes says Steam is not running (error 113, "please reinstall") although it is. Fully close BCD and start the game again. This build logs what the launcher sees, to find the cause.
- Very long GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 sessions can stop when the emulator's memory area is full. Fully close BCD (swipe it away) and start again.
- Enshrouded and Hades II stop with a Steam "version mismatch": their Steam library is newer than the Steam client BCD Dock runs.
- The foldable iPhone's tabletop pose is in the code, but this build cannot read the hinge yet (it needs a newer iOS SDK).
- Windows Vulkan is new and tried on few games.

**Thanks** to @rbarton124, @pauloec, @iqui27, @creeper4004 and @Taala2 for their contributions to this release, and to Mila (mudcatpot) for the new icon.

Install help, game reports and ideas: join the [BCD-Games Discord](https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug).

**BCD.ipa**: the unsigned IPA, for sideloading with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. It needs iOS 18 or later and JIT; the README has the details.
**BCD-source.tar.xz**: the complete source of this build with all its submodules (GPL-3.0).

apps.name: iDeck
apps.subtitle: Steam Big Picture on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription:
# Steam64 setup, one step at a time

**Experimental prerelease · Build145 · Known issue: Steam can freeze after the third game exit. This update improves setup; it does not fix that stability issue.**

## What’s new

- **Install Steam64 in the launcher:** downloads the matched Steam/browser packages from Valve over HTTPS, verifies sizes/SHA-256 and installs with rollback. Cancel/retry, Verify/Repair and Return to previous environment are available.
- **Four clear actions:** Install Steam → Connect LocalDevVPN → Pair this device → Enable JIT. Runtime preparation is automatic, signing/address checks remain mandatory, completed steps are checked/skipped and the view follows the next action.
- **Pair in iDeck:** starts the existing on-device pairing immediately with live instructions/PIN, without hunting through JIT settings. iOS calls the pairing host Madeira. Advanced methods/import/recovery/account/auto-start settings are collapsed.
- **Data stays yours:** the original environment remains intact; no auth cache, game or save is silently transferred. Use Valve’s own login and Steam Guard yourself.

## Install and test

Download `iDeck-0.1.3-alpha.6-build145.ipa` and `SHA256SUMS`, verify the hash, then sign/sideload using your own coherent development main/helper profiles. Keep `MadeiraJITHelper.appex` and debugging permission; signing alone does not activate JIT. Back up saves and keep the same app identity when upgrading—uninstalling can erase local data.

Open iDeck and follow the highlighted setup step; fully close/reopen when prompted after installing Steam64. For on-device pairing use iOS27; iOS26 offers pairing-file import. Activate JIT again for each new app process.

The IPA includes the local runtime and pinned source-built open support components, **no Valve Steam client/libcef, games, accounts, maintainer profile or pairing file**. The installer acquires the client from Valve. Both source companions, relink, license/audit and inventory/checksum assets accompany this release.

## What was verified

The user reports Build144 installation can complete. Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Game support remains experimental.

## Download

**[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.2.0/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)**

Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and games you own. You only need the IPA to install; supply your own game files or download owned games from Steam.

## Install

1. Sign and install the IPA and helper with a compatible sideloading tool, or import it into LiveContainer using its supported JIT setup.
2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**.
3. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**.

For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation.

Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. Keep that older folder until you have checked your saves.

## What's new

- **Steam downloads in the app.** Sign in with a password or QR code, with Steam Guard support, browse your library, and choose download language, unprotected branch, 32/64-bit files, and owned DLC.
- **A download queue with verification and repair.** Pause, resume, retry, and prioritize downloads. Check for updates or repair downloaded files while keeping the previous installation.
- **Clearer storage warnings.** Download checks use the space available to Iridium and account for verified partial files. **Download Anyway** can bypass an estimated-space warning for one attempt; file verification and real out-of-space errors remain enforced.
- **Updated Windows runtime.** Includes 32-bit WoW64 support and D3D9/D3D12 updates. Support still varies by game and device.
- **Game prerequisite installers.** Run supported setup steps included with a game, or choose **Game Options → Run Installer** for an EXE or MSI installer you provide. Some installers need interaction. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required.
- **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them.

## Known issues

- Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, input, save, or shutdown problems. Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified.
- Keep Iridium open while downloading. Downloads pause when the app goes into the background and need to be resumed. Real-account downloads and recovery after Wi-Fi or network loss still need device testing.
- Steam Cloud, Workshop, Steam Families library discovery, password-protected branches, and desktop Steam services are not included. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading.
- Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving.
- JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. Built-in JIT requires standalone Iridium, debugging permission, a valid pairing file, and LocalDevVPN. Hosted Iridium uses external JIT. Recipient signing, LiveContainer hosting, and game prerequisite success still need device testing.

<details>
<summary>Source code, licenses, and build details</summary>

## Source and licenses

The other release files are for source access, rebuilding, and download verification:

- Download both `Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01` and `.part02` for the complete matching source package.
- `Iridium-source-guide.zip` contains license notices, source records, and build/relink instructions.
- `SHA256SUMS` verifies the IPA, both source parts, and the source guide.

Download all five release files into one folder, then run:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
cat Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01 Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part02 > Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz
unzip Iridium-source-guide.zip
shasum -a 256 -c Iridium-source-guide/ASSEMBLED-SHA256SUMS
```

The source guide includes the assembled archive's checksum and rebuild instructions. Keep the matching source and guide beside the IPA at this versioned release URL. GitHub's automatic repository ZIP does not contain all required dependency sources.

Source commit: b7e24f9fb4dd17f5d940c4763123f2b00d0e121f
Build run: https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/actions/runs/37142663989

App and helper version: **0.2.0 (115.1)**, minimum iOS **18.0**, confirmed in the actual delivered Info.plist files. The IPA is **399,916,792 bytes**; SHA-256 `1934922a1fcf1509e305a29d6f0d26579a4318ba95dfcf5b406d5e38f88c9763`.

Source checks, Steam native/simulator checks, the full app build, and final binary/package checks passed. Independent IPA inspection confirmed the exact anonymous XML/DER entitlement carrier with no CMS payload or team identity, eight unsigned non-main native binaries, strict bundle verification, runtime hashes, and ZIP modes and symlinks. Unchanged runtime component outputs were reused after provenance checks. These checks do not establish real-account login, owned-game downloads, game compatibility, recipient signing, or physical-device behavior.

Apple compiler-runtime notice uncertainty and unsigned-IPA contractual authorization remain documented risks. Retain the license guide in `Iridium-source-guide.zip`.

</details>
